outcome: Permission and job notifications now tell the truth plainly. Approving something once says so — 'Approved for this run only; future runs will need approval again' — instead of leaving you to discover the difference later. A job that finishes despite a blocked step sends ONE card ('Completed with limits', naming what degraded and every one-time approval) instead of a green Completed and an orange Setup-needed contradicting each other, and no path can leave a paused job silent. A command blocked because its shape didn't match shows the approved pattern next to what was attempted — ending the 'was it even granted?' guessing from the incident. And a repeating permission prompt now says how many times you've approved it and over how many days, offering to make it permanent.
